title: Babur Marks Diwali With Five-Course Tasting Menu in Forest Hill
excerpt: The Forest Hill restaurant serves Head Chef Jiwan Lal's five-course Diwali menu from 6 to 8 November 2026, at £64.95, with a £74.95 candlelit party on the final night.
body:
• Babur in Forest Hill, London, serves a five-course Diwali tasting menu from Friday 6 to Sunday 8 November 2026, created by Head Chef Jiwan Lal.
  • The menu costs £64.95 per person, with an optional wine flight for £30; the candlelit Diwali Party on Sunday 8 November costs £74.95 including live entertainment.
  • Courses run from Delhi-style ram laddu chaat and Malvani fish tikka to chicken anarkali, palak paneer kofta and khoya gujiya with saffron yoghurt ice cream.
  • Babur is at 119 Brockley Rise, Forest Hill, London SE23 1JP; bookings are via the restaurant on 020 8291 2400.

Babur, the Forest Hill Indian restaurant that has traded for 41 years, will mark Diwali with a five-course tasting menu served over three nights, from Friday 6 to Sunday 8 November 2026. The menu, created by Head Chef Jiwan Lal, is built around regional Indian dishes and seasonal ingredients, according to Foodepedia, which first reported the programme.

What is on the menu

The meal opens with a Delhi-style ram laddu chaat — crisp moong dal fritters with grated radish, mint chutney and sweet tamarind — paired in the restaurant's listing with a German Riesling. A Malvani fish tikka follows, using char-grilled wild salmon with coastal Malvani spices and a smoked coconut chutney, paired with an Alsace Pinot Blanc.

The two main courses are served as the centre of the menu. Chicken anarkali is described as tender chicken in a gravy of saffron, almonds and cashews. Alongside it, palak paneer kofta pairs paneer dumplings with a creamy spinach sauce and aromatic spices, giving vegetarian diners a main course designed for the menu rather than substituted into it.

Dessert is khoya gujiya, a flaky pastry filled with reduced milk, nuts and spices, served with saffron yoghurt ice cream. Gujiya is a Diwali staple in many north Indian homes, and Babur's version keeps the festive sweet at the centre while presenting it in tasting-menu form.

Prices, party night and booking details

The tasting menu is priced at £64.95 per person, with an optional wine flight at £30, Foodepedia reported. The programme ends on Sunday 8 November with a candlelit Diwali Party that combines the full menu with live performances, priced at £74.95 per person.

An independent London Diwali guide from DesignMyNight lists the same dates and the same two prices, and adds that the party ticket includes a welcome drink and entertainment, with live Bollywood dancing. The guide places Babur second in its round-up of London Diwali events for 2026.

Babur is at 119 Brockley Rise, Forest Hill, London SE23 1JP. The restaurant's own site is linked from the Foodepedia listing as babur.info, and the listing gives the booking telephone number as 020 8291 2400.

Why it matters for London diners

Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November in 2026, so Babur's three-night run covers the festival weekend itself rather than a date weeks away from it. For south London's Indian diaspora, the offer is specific: a neighbourhood restaurant with a four-decade history, a regional menu that moves from Delhi chaat to Maharashtra's Malvan coast, and a party night for families who want the celebration handled for them.

London has larger Diwali set menus this year at higher prices in central London. Babur's pitch is different — a local institution in Forest Hill doing a focused, five-course version at £64.95. With only three nights and a single party evening, early booking is the practical step for readers who want the Sunday night.
